_meta.purpose: Indicative government circle-rate price band per PIN, shown in Rs/sq ft for buyers.
_meta.circle_rate_note: 'Circle rate' and 'collector rate' are the SAME thing — the government's minimum property value, used to calculate stamp duty and registration charges. Delhi/UP call it circle rate; Haryana calls it collector rate.
_meta.unit_note: All figures converted to Rs per sq ft. rate_sqft is the apartment/built-up band a buyer would see; land_sqft (where present) is the government plot/land rate per sq ft. Exact where rate_exact/land_exact is true (Delhi land categories, Noida sectors, Indirapuram); indicative bands elsewhere.
_meta.market_gap_note: Actual market prices in NCR typically run 20–70% ABOVE the circle rate (highest in prime Delhi & Gurugram, per Anarock/industry data). The circle rate is only the legal floor — budget for the difference in your own funds, since home loans are usually capped near this valuation.
_meta.disclaimer: Government minimum valuation, not market price. Figures are indicative Rs/sq ft bands unless marked exact, and a single PIN can span cheaper and pricier pockets. Not part of the NQI score.

sources.bangalore: Karnataka guidance value — Kaveri portal, Dept. of Stamps & Registration
sources.punjab: Punjab collector rate (Sub Registrar/Tehsil rate lists), 2025-26 — quoted per sq yd in source, converted ÷9 to Rs/sq ft

_meta.punjab_unit_note: Punjab collector rates are notified per square YARD, not per square foot like Delhi/Bangalore — converted here (÷9) for a consistent display unit. A single named locality can span more than one priced row in the source document; the row cited is the best match, not necessarily every parcel in the area.
